title: bot: expand module (train settlers, found new villages)
criteria:
Add the `expand` bot module (T24 part a). All code in English, no Thai text. Bots act only through services. Config already has `PersonalityDef.expand_radius` (int, default 8), cfg.culture (village_cp_thresholds, settlers_needed), cfg.units['settler'] (trained_in palace, requires palace 10), and personalities have weights['expand'].
EDITING RULE: realm/bot/action.py, modules.py and brain.py already exist: use small targeted Edit operations (append the new function / add one branch / extend the registries); do not rewrite whole files.
== realm/bot/action.py ==
Add the kind 'settle' to `Action.execute`: military.send_troops(s, bot.id, village.id, params['to_x'], params['to_y'], Mission.SETTLE, params['units'], now, cfg). Update the kind comment.
== realm/bot/brain.py ==
Register the module: `modules.expand` goes into `_MODULES` and 'expand' -> 'expand' into `_WEIGHT_KEYS` (the weight key is personality.weights['expand']). Nothing else changes.
== realm/bot/modules.py ==
`expand(ctx: BotContext) -> list[Action]`: returns [] unless the bot is allowed a new village: pending = count of Movement rows with player_id == bot.id, mission 'settle' and status 'moving'; need = villages.culture_needed_for_next_village(ctx.s, ctx.bot, ctx.cfg, extra_pending=pending); need is None or villages.projected_culture(ctx.s, ctx.bot, ctx.now, ctx.cfg) < need -> []. needed = cfg.culture.settlers_needed. A) when ctx.troops_home.get('settler', 0) >= needed: target = `_find_settle_tile(ctx)`; none -> []; else one Action kind 'settle', score 4.0, params {'to_x', 'to_y', 'units': {'settler': needed}}, module 'expand'. B) otherwise try to train settlers: return [] when units.missing_unit_requirements('settler', ctx.levels, cfg) is non-empty, or when a TrainingQueue row with unit 'settler' exists for this village, or when the player already has >= needed settlers anywhere (sum of Troop.count of unit 'settler' with home_village_id == village.id, any location) or in moving settle movements; cost = units.unit_cost('settler', bot.tribe, cfg).scale(needed); when the village stock does not cover it (Res.covers) return []; else one Action kind 'train', score 3.5, params {'unit': 'settler', 'count': needed}, module 'expand'.
`_find_settle_tile(ctx) -> tuple[int, int] | None`: radius = ctx.personality.expand_radius; candidate tiles = Tile rows of the world with kind 'valley' inside the square box of +-radius around the village (use realm.core.movement.wrap for x/y so the torus edge works; query with x IN / y IN lists) whose torus distance (movement.distance with world.size) from the village is between 1 and radius inclusive; exclude tiles that already hold a village, tiles that are the destination (to_x, to_y) of ANY moving settle movement in the world, and tiles closer than cfg.world.min_village_distance to ANY village of the world (query the villages in the box extended by min_village_distance); choose the candidate with the smallest (distance, x, y); None when there is none. Use ONE query for tiles, ONE for villages, ONE for the settle movements.
== tests/bot/test_expand.py ==
DB fixtures `s`, `cfg`, `t0`; world = worlds.create_world(s, seed=1, speed=1, player_name='ผู้เล่น', tribe='stonehold', bot_count=2, cfg=cfg, real_now=t0). Use bot 1 with tribe forced to 'stonehold', its village moved to (30, 30) (other villages are elsewhere), personality 'farmer' via the profile, culture forced with direct writes on the Player (culture_points, cp_updated_at = now). A clean patch: set every Tile of the box x in 24..36, y in 24..36 to kind 'lake' except valleys at (32, 30) (distance 2), (30, 33) (distance 3) and (31, 30) (distance 1 but excluded below); ensure there is no village in the box other than the bot's. Hand-computed cases: (1) culture 2000 (needed for the 2nd village), palace level 10 in the village (Building at center slot 22), Troop(home=village, location=village, 'settler', 3): expand() returns exactly one action kind 'settle', score 4.0, params to (31, 30) when (31,30) is a valid valley and no village is within min_village_distance 3 ... NOTE min_village_distance is 3, so with the bot village at (30,30) only tiles at distance >= 3 qualify: therefore (32,30) at distance 2 and (31,30) at distance 1 are EXCLUDED and the answer is (30, 33) (distance 3); make the test expect (30, 33); a valley at distance 5 (e.g. (35, 30)) is also present and loses to (30, 33). (2) culture 1999.9 -> []. (3) no settlers and palace level 0 -> [] (requirements). (4) no settlers, palace level 10, stock set to 9000 each: one action kind 'train', score 3.5, params {'unit': 'settler', 'count': 3}; with stock 100 each -> []; with a TrainingQueue row (building 'palace', unit 'settler', count_total 3) -> []; with Troop(home=village, location=another village, 'settler', 3) -> []. (5) with a moving settle Movement of this player already present the needed culture becomes 8000 -> [] at culture 2000. (6) a valley that already holds a village or is the target of another moving settle Movement is skipped (use (30, 33) as the occupied one -> the next candidate (35, 30) is chosen). (7) tile search wraps around the torus edge: bot village at (50, 0) with a valley at (-49, 0)... distance 2 is < 3 so use (-48, 0) at distance 3 (50 -> -48 is 99 apart on size 101 -> torus distance 3): chosen when the only valley around is there. (8) Action.execute('settle') calls send_troops: with rally_point level 1 in slot 39 and the tile (30, 33) valley, the settle Movement exists afterwards (mission 'settle', units {'settler': 3}, to (30, 33)). (9) brain integration: with culture, settlers and tile ready a 'farmer' (weights expand 0.3) personality at difficulty 'hard' returns the settle action among executed actions of brain.think (hard: max_actions 6, skip_chance 0) and a Movement mission 'settle' exists.
notes:
- Real columns only in tests: Player.culture_points/cp_updated_at, Tile.kind/layout, Village.x/y, Building, Troop, TrainingQueue, Movement.
- Moving the village: update village.x, village.y (UNIQUE world_id,x,y - make sure the target coordinates are free).
- Never commit; never call datetime.now(); the module must not mutate anything (read-only).
- Existing tests must keep passing.
